purpose: LRM 9.15 sourceScaleFactor: source stepping solves an operating point plain Newton and gmin stepping do not

oracle.derivation: 5 V through 1 ohm into is*(exp(v/vt) - 1), is = 1e-14, vt = 0.025, no $limit. From the cold start Newton's first iterate is near 5 V and each step comes down about vt: ~165 steps to the knee, past plain Newton's 100 iterations and each gmin step's 50, so the operating point needs source stepping. The root of (5 - v)/1 = 1e-14*(exp(v/0.025) - 1) is V(a) = 0.8415334423073747 (Newton in python3); V(in) = 5. No charge, so every transient row repeats it. At t = 0 the published point is Newton's last linearization point, inside SPICE's reltol of the root (atol 1e-3); each transient point re-solves from the last, so samples inside the run are held to 1e-6. A factor left at 0.9375 gives 0.83959.
